questions.question: What is meant by a free-turbine turboshaft engine?
questions.idealAnswer: A turboshaft engine that has a turbine wheel, or stage of turbine wheels, that is not used to drive the compressor of the gas generator section of the engine. This free turbine drives the propeller in a turboprop engine or the transmission and rotor of a helicopter.

questions.question: What is meant by a hung start in a turbine engine?
questions.idealAnswer: A start in which ignition occurs, but the engine does not accelerate to a self-sustaining speed.

questions.question: What is meant by a hot start in a turbine engine?
questions.idealAnswer: A start in which ignition occurs, but the internal temperatures go high enough that they can damage the engine.

questions.question: What is meant by creep of the turbine blades?
questions.idealAnswer: A condition of permanent elongation of the turbine blades. Creep is caused by the high temperatures and the high centrifugal loading imposed on the blades.

questions.question: How is the compressor of a turbine engine cleaned?
questions.idealAnswer: An emulsion-type cleaner is sprayed through the engine while it is being motored by the starter or operated at a low speed. The wash is followed by a clean water rinse. More vigorous cleaning is done by injecting a mild abrasive, such as ground-up apricot pits or walnut shells, into the engine while it is operating at low speed.
